page: Amazon Web Services c8g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 design running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and includes a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory bandwidth. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation with Clang. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with both cached and uncached read-only memory bandwidth tests placing in the top 10% tier. Additionally, the instance demonstrates top-tier throughput in static web serving, Redis SET operations, and Passmark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8g.16xlarge leverages custom ARM-based silicon to deliver high resource density and compute throughput per unit of resource, making it highly competitive for scale-out workloads compared to traditional architectures. Given its compute-heavy profile and high memory bandwidth, this instance is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and database operations.
